Gangamma W/O Late Ramanna vs Pankaj Menaria S/O Puran Mal Ji on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18549644/
1  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11478  MFA No. 100142 of 2021  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
The claimants are in appeal seeking for higher compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 02.03.2020, passed in MVC No.954/2018 on the file of the MACT No.XI and Second Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge at Ballari.

2. Smt. Soubhagya Vakkund for Shri Y.Lakshmikant Reddy appearing for the appellants submits that the Triubnal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased and had awarded meager compensation on all other heads.
Hence, she seeks to allow the appeal.
3. Per contra, learned counsel Shry M.Y. Katagi appearing for respondent No.2 supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and seeks for dismissal of the appeal.
4. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the materials available on record.
The pleadings and evidence on record indicate that the road traffic accident which occurred on 27.02.2018 and due to such accident, the husband and father of the claimants succumbed to the injuries.
The deceased was aged about 47 years at the time of accident.
No evidence is placed on record with regard to the income of the deceased.
Hence, this Court reassess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.11,750/- p.m. placing reliance on the Notional Income Chart prepared by the KSLSA.
25% of the assessed income is added under the head loss of future prospects.
Thus, the loss of dependency is reassessed at Rs.15,27,500/- (Rs.11,750/- + 25% x 12 x 13 x 2/3rd).

6. Further, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses and transportation of dead body with 10% escalation.

7. In terms of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited NC: 2024:KHC-D:11478 Vs. Nanu Ram & Others1, the appellants would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of consortium' with 10% escalation.

Loss of dependency Rs.15,27,500/-

2  Loss of estate Rs.16,500/-
 Funeral expenses  & transportation of dead body Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of consortium Rs.88,000/-
 ------------------
 Total Rs.16,48,500/-
 ------------------
2.

In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal stands partly allowed.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the claimants are entitled to total 2018 ACJ 2782 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11478 compensation of Rs.16,48,500/- as against Rs.11,00,052/- awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
(iv) The respondents shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(v) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made in terms of award of the Tribunal.

(vi) Registry to draw modified award accordingly.
(vii) No costs.

Sd/-
